blocks.text: The chapter moves from Jerusalem under siege and a dramatic Day of Jehovah—including divine combat, a divided Mount of Olives, escape, and altered light—to a picture of living waters flowing from Jerusalem in every season, Jehovah’s universal kingship, and a secure inhabited city. Its closing movement includes judgment on hostile nations, then surviving nations coming annually to worship and keep the Feast of Tabernacles; holiness extends even to horses’ bells and ordinary cooking pots.

Verse 5 compares the people’s flight with a remembered earthquake in Uzziah’s days. Amos 1:1 also recalls an earthquake as a chronological marker, but neither text supplies an absolute year. Proposed links to particular archaeological destruction layers remain uncertain, so the reference should not be treated as securely identifying its date, magnitude, epicenter, or physical remains.
